subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value:
THE `__unexpected` ISLAND'S EH-STATE FRAME SLOT IS ALLOCATED BY THE COMPILER OUTSIDE THE USER LOCAL BLOCK, SO IT IS NOT MOVABLE BY ANY PADDING-LOCAL SHAPE, SIZE OR DECLARATION POSITION -- AND slotdiff CANNOT SEE IT. Split the residual in two before spending probes, because the two halves have different answers.

HALF ONE, THE FRAME SIZE, IS SOURCE-REACHABLE and yields to the ordinary padding-local idiom: fndiff --clean's `HINT: frame delta +N -> try u8 unused[N]` was correct twice here (fn_800D9C5C 64 -> 72, fn_800D96B0 64 -> 72), each closing several real diff lines including the `lwz r0,K(r31)` and `lmw r28,K(r12)` epilogue displacements.

HALF TWO, THE ISLAND'S OWN SLOT, IS NOT. After the frame is byte-correct, the island can still read `addi r3,r31,24` against a target `addi r3,r31,32` -- an 8-byte delta INSIDE a frame whose total size, saved-register set and complete r1 occupancy map are all already identical. Four distinct probes failed to move it: pad declared first, pad declared last, pad hoisted into a trailing nested block, and pad respelled as an 8-byte `f64`. Two of those were on one function and two on another, so this is not a single function's quirk.

WHY THE USUAL ARBITER IS BLIND HERE, which is the part worth carrying: slotdiff collects r1 displacements from loads/stores and from `addi rX,r1,N` address-takes, and it reported SLOT MAP IDENTICAL for all three functions while this delta was live. The island's `addi r3,r31,K` is taken off the FRAME POINTER r31, not off r1, so it never enters the occupancy map. A SLOT MAP IDENTICAL verdict is therefore evidence about the user local block only, and says nothing about EH-state placement -- do not read it as 'the frame is fully solved'.

OPERATIONAL RULE. On any function carrying an `__unexpected` island, close the frame size with the padding idiom, then read the island's `addi rN,r31,K` displacement DIRECTLY out of the aligned view as a separate residual. If it disagrees while the slot map is identical, stop: it is not a locals problem. Record it and move on rather than cycling padding shapes -- three functions in this TU (fn_800D9C5C real 4, fn_800D96B0 real 8, and dtor_800DBB94's sibling `mr r12,r31` epilogue tiebreak) sit on exactly this wall with instruction counts exact and opcode multisets IDENTICAL.
